From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Acme redlines — legal guidance

Sergio / Priyom — I've reviewed the redlines. High-level: most changes are reasonable and align with prior customers; we should accept except for two items we should push back on:

1) Section 6.2 (Indemnity): Acme added a reciprocal carve-out for consequential damages that is broader than standard. Recommend we keep our existing language but offer a narrow clarification that preserves mutual limitation of liability; I can draft a one-line replacement.
2) Data retention appendix: they requested 7 years for logs. Our standard is 1 year for operational logs and 3 years for billing records. If sales wants to accept 7 years, ops/infra needs to confirm cost impact. Prefer to counter to 3 years.

Execution plan:
- I can produce a clean MSA with our proposed notes (I will also prepare a one-paragraph summary for Acme counsel).
- DocuSign routing: Recommend two envelopes to keep things clear — Envelope A: MSA (signed by Acme CFO -> Redwood CEO). Envelope B: Order Form (signed by Acme Procurement -> Redwood Account Exec). That keeps approval/PO tracking straightforward.

On signer authority: Accepting "CFO or delegated authority" is fine — ask them to confirm the actual signer's name and email for DocuSign. For countersignature, Redwood requires CEO signature on the MSA and the RW Account Exec signature on Order Form per our internal policy for deals above $250k.

I'll attach the clean copy once I finish edits.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
